place.en: A Lalbaug chawl · twenty minutes of load-shedding · 10:40 PM

brief.en: The lights went out over Feeder 4 for twenty minutes and room 14 was emptied of a family’s gold. The whole wing stood in the corridor in the dark. Somebody worked by a light nobody else had.

iraNote.en: “Everyone in that corridor was in the dark. Find the one who wasn’t.”

text.en: Feeder 4, 10:40 to 11:00. Posted on the 3rd. Feeder 4 is this wing.
A cracked lens off a long-barrel torch. Meter readers carry them. Nobody in this chawl does.
The hasp is unbent and the screws are bright. The plate came off and went back on.
Read on the 1st. Read again on the 3rd. Nobody reads a meter twice in three days.
Lalbaug to Byculla, punched 11:12 — twelve minutes after the lights came back.
Crow. That grille has been a roost for years.

dismissNote.en: ruled out — the birds were here first

text.en: Two neighbours argued about the water tap for the whole twenty minutes. Nine people heard every word.

dismissNote.en: ruled out — loud is not guilty, and it alibis two of them

text.en: One chappal, size nine, left on the half-landing.

dismissNote.en: ruled out — half the chawl leaves chappals on that landing

hook.en: knows the feeder schedule by heart

confession.en: He read room 14 twice in three days to be sure of what was in it, unscrewed the hasp plate in the dark by his own torch, and was on a bus to Byculla twelve minutes after the lights came back.

alibi.en: Shouting about the water tap for the entire twenty minutes, in front of nine people.

hook.en: the stairwell is his to watch

alibi.en: In the corridor with everyone else, holding the only lantern the wing owns — which is why nobody could work by it.
The other half of the water-tap argument. Nine witnesses, and his mother’s gold.

correction.en: A chappal is not a motive. A meter read twice in three days is somebody counting what’s inside.
Everybody had the dark. One man had a torch, and he left the glass of it on the landing.
Nobody escapes through a window grille. There was a bus to Byculla at 11:12 and somebody was on it.

text.en: “Nobody in this wing owns a torch. The lantern is the wing’s, and it was in my hand.”
“A query. The tenant said the units were wrong.” No such complaint is on file.

setting.en: The stairwell, holding the wing’s one lantern.

ask.en: Twenty minutes of dark. What did you see?

answer.en: “The corridor, by my own lamp. Everyone was in it and everyone was shouting.”

note.en: Everyone in the corridor. So room 14 was worked on by somebody who wasn’t.

ask.en: There is a torch lens on the landing. Whose torch?

answer.en: “Not mine. I carry a lantern — the wing bought it because nobody here can afford batteries.”

lockedHint.en: Pin the torch glass. He cannot answer for a lens you have not decided matters.

note.en: Nobody here can afford batteries. So the torch came from outside the wing.

ask.en: Who comes into this building who doesn’t live in it?

answer.en: “Post, milk, and the meter man. The meter man has the stairwell key.”

note.en: That is a short list, and it just got shorter.

setting.en: The depot at Byculla, on his break, with his bag on his knees.

answer.en: “That’s the cycle. Every flat, first of the month.”

note.en: The cycle, then. Which makes the second reading the one to ask about.

ask.en: You read it again on the 3rd.

answer.en: “A query. The tenant said the units were wrong.”

lockedHint.en: Pin the meter card — two readings in three days is the whole question.

note.en: A query nobody in room 14 raised. There is no complaint on any book.

answer.en: “On the 11:12 to Byculla. You can see the punch.”

note.en: You can. Twelve minutes after the lights came back, from a stop four minutes’ walk away.

text.en: The cut was posted on the 3rd, and room 14’s meter was read on the 3rd. Who reads the board and the meter?
